title: Inverse image of the regular ring-sheaf module, with unit compatibility
statement: Let f:X→Y be a continuous map of topological spaces and R a sheaf of commutative rings on Y. Give f⁻¹R the regular module structure and give the additive inverse image of the regular R-module the canonical inverseImageModule action [def-pc-topological-inverse-image-module]. There exists an f⁻¹R-linear isomorphism e:f⁻¹(Reg R) ≅ Reg(f⁻¹R). For every open V of Y and d∈R(V), e on f⁻¹V carries the additive inverse-image unit of d to the ring inverse-image unit of d. The construction includes empty spaces, empty opens and zero rings.

source.place: Tag 008X and its presheaf-inverse-image and sheafification construction; Tags 008T and 0089

proof.text: The forgetful functor CommRingCat→RingCat→AddCommGrpCat preserves filtered colimits and the limits used in sheafification. The costructured-arrow categories for the opposite Opens.map f are filtered, via representable flatness of Opens.map f. Mathlib leftKanExtensionCompIsoOfPreserves therefore identifies the additive presheaf inverse image of R with the underlying additive presheaf of the ring inverse image. Sheafify this isomorphism and compose with sheafifyComposeIso to obtain the canonical additive sheaf isomorphism q.

Expand the constructed inverse-image adjunction unit as the Lan unit followed by the sheafification unit. The inverse factorization formula for leftKanExtensionCompIsoOfPreserves, naturality of toSheafify, and sheafComposeIso_hom_fac show that q sends each additive unit image of d to the corresponding ring unit image.

Compare q(r•m) and r*q(m). The canonical inverse-image module action is restriction-compatible and its unit is semilinear. Naturality of q and multiplicativity of ring restriction show both operations commute with restriction. On pairs of unit images the semilinear unit law, the preceding unit formula, and multiplicativity of the ring unit identify the operations. Apply inverseImageOperation_ext to obtain the equality everywhere.

Bundle q as a linear map with PresheafOfModules.homMk. The inverse is linear by applying the injective q to the scalar-linearity equation and using q inverse identities. The additive inverse identities become the module inverse identities by extensionality. The unit formula already proved for q gives the claimed formula for this module isomorphism.

theorem exists_inverseImage_regularModule_iso :
    ∃ e : inverseImageModule f R (SheafOfModules.unit (𝓡 R)) ≅
      SheafOfModules.unit (𝓡 (inverseImageRing f R)),
      ∀ (V : (Opens Y)ᵒᵖ) (d : R.obj.obj V),
        e.hom.val.app ((Opens.map f).op.obj V)
          (((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafAdjunctionContinuous
            (Opens.map f) AddCommGrpCat.{u} (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y)
            (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)).unit.app
              ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (𝓡 R)).obj
                (SheafOfModules.unit (𝓡 R)))).hom.app V d) =
          ((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafAdjunctionContinuous
            (Opens.map f) CommRingCat.{u} (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y)
            (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)).unit.app R).hom.app V d
